newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar resumes downtrend, spread eases.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar resumes downtrend, spread eases.

text.p: White sugar futures extended this week's downward trend on Thursday as a mixed bag of players moved out of spot August but the hefty volume mainly derived from crossed and AA trades.
Commission houses and trade houses provided the bulk of the August trading, which accounted for most of the session's turnover of 1,108 lots by 1100 GMT.
The August/October spread also attracted dealing interest, narrowing to $3.20 at one stage. It later widened out to $3.50 where broker buying was noted.
At Wednesday's close August/October was nominally valued at $3.80.
Traders said the spread was likely to widen further as outright August firmed on account of the widespread talk in the market of untenderable sugars hedged against August by the trade.
August was down $1.50 at $317.50 and October down $1.10 at $314.10. Other positions also lost ground.
Technical analysts said August's move below $320 suggested that prices could again challenge support at around $315.50, at the upward trendline extending from January's low of $295.00.
In fundamental news, administrative portworkers at Santos decided to end their strike and return to work at 0400 GMT after loading and unloading operations were paralysed at public berths.
Paris was subdued with just 87 lots trading on the 45 ICUMSA market. August was down 70 cents at $317.70 and October flat at $314.50. No trades were posted on the 100 ICUMSA market.
